title: Chinese car sales double in Europe as Chinese brands account for one in seven new cars
html:
Chinese car brands continue to grow rapidly in Europe. In October, 151,112 new passenger cars from Chinese brands were registered across Europe, up 103% on a year earlier. Their market share reached 13.6%. The growing popularity of hybrids is providing the biggest boost, while established European carmakers face increasingly fierce competition.

Hybrids become the biggest driver of growth for Chinese carmakers

Sales of Chinese car brands more than doubled year on year in October, according to market research firm Dataforce. Their market share fell short of September’s record 14.5%, but was still among the highest on record.

Hybrid sales are growing particularly quickly. Registrations of hybrids from Chinese brands rose 182% year on year, accounting for more than a quarter of all hybrid car sales in Europe.

The success of Chinese carmakers is partly down to European Union trade policy. Additional tariffs have applied to electric cars made in China since 2024, but they do not apply to hybrids in the same way.

As a result, BYD, Chery and other manufacturers have expanded their plug-in hybrid ranges, offering buyers the option of driving on electric power while retaining the longer range of a petrol engine.

BYD, Chery and Leapmotor record the fastest growth

Leapmotor was among the biggest gainers, with EU registrations up 279.3% year on year in October. Chery grew by 184.7% and BYD by 128.1%.

BYD registered 30,974 cars in the EU in October, nearly three times Tesla’s 10,166.

Chery Group, whose brands include Omoda and Jaecoo, reached 21,458 registrations. Leapmotor registered 11,709 vehicles.

Models driving the growth include the BYD Seal U DM-i, the Jaecoo 7 SHS and Leapmotor’s affordable electric cars.

For buyers, the expansion of Chinese brands means a wider choice of models, particularly among electric cars and plug-in hybrids. Alongside competitive pricing, these cars often come well equipped as standard, but the reach of service networks and the aftersales experience vary by brand.

European carmakers feel the pressure

The rapid growth of Chinese brands comes as several major European carmakers post weaker sales figures.

In October, new car registrations in the EU fell by 9% for Volkswagen Group, 8.5% for Renault Group and 7% for Stellantis.

That does not mean all those buyers chose Chinese models over European cars. But the figures show that Chinese carmakers are gaining market share while several established competitors are losing it.

In the third quarter, Chinese brands overtook Japanese brands in Europe for the first time, taking a 12.7% market share against 11.9% for their Japanese rivals.

Five years ago, Chinese brands accounted for only about one per cent of European car sales.

Chinese carmakers set up factories in Europe

Rapid sales growth is also prompting Chinese companies to rethink their manufacturing strategies.

BYD is building a car plant in Hungary and is in talks to buy Ineos’s Hambach factory in France.

Chery is preparing to start production in Barcelona, while Leapmotor has begun building its electric B10 SUV at Stellantis’s plant in Zaragoza, Spain.

Manufacturing in Europe would help cut transport costs and reduce the impact of tariffs on electric cars imported from China.

Meanwhile, the EU is preparing to restrict imports of Chinese hybrid cars. The measures, which take effect in December, are intended to curb the rapid growth in imports and protect Europe’s car industry.

The growth of Chinese carmakers shows that the balance of power in Europe’s car market is shifting significantly. Brands that were relatively unknown just a few years ago are now competing directly with Volkswagen, Renault and other major carmakers.

For consumers, this could mean more choice and stronger price competition. For European carmakers, it means pressure to bring new models to market faster and give buyers more for the same money.
summary: Chinese brands registered 151,112 new passenger cars across Europe in October, up 103% year on year and taking a 13.6% market share, with hybrids providing the biggest boost.
